version.note: The performing edition and any cuts or retouchings by the conductor are not identified in the sources consulted.

date.note: Bolig dates all three sides of the first movement (CVE-29052, -29053 and -29054) to 28 April 1927. The Internet Archive description and Pristine give the two session days (28 and 30 April 1927) for the symphony as a whole.

place.value: Academy of Music, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States

label.note: Stokowski’s earlier acoustic recording of 1924 used the same matrix numbers without the CVE prefix and different issue numbers (Bolig lists 74894–74897 and 6459–6460); this transfer is the electrical recording of 1927 by its description, session dates and Victor numbers.

catalogue.note: The Internet Archive description says “Originally issued as Victor 6663, 6664 & 6665. (Later as a set as M-16.)”; Pristine gives the same numbers and album. Bolig also lists later Victor and HMV issues of the same sides. The disc and side on which the movement boundary falls are not identified; the allocation of matrices to movements follows Bolig’s part numbers.

matrixTakeSides.value: Parts 1–3: CVE-29052, take 6; CVE-29053, take 6; CVE-29054, take 6
matrixTakeSides.note: Bolig and the Pristine producer’s note agree on the matrices and takes of the first movement. The DAHR matrix pages could not be opened on 17 October 2026 (503 error). No run-out inspection has been made of the digital surrogate.

credits.note: The Internet Archive description reads “Transfer by Bob Varney”.

date.note: No transfer date is identified. The Internet Archive item was added on 24 January 2011, which is an upload date.

processing.note: The stylus, equalisation, speed and noise treatment are not documented. The file runs 10:28; Pristine’s own restoration runs 10:33, so the two transfers differ by a few seconds, and where the side joins fall in this file is not known.

digital.format: Uploader-supplied MP3, classified as the original file by the Internet Archive (encoding history unknown); the Archive’s Ogg Vorbis file is its derivative

composition.value: Underlying composition is out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies.
composition.note: Schubert died in 1828. This is a term calculation, not a worldwide clearance or a statement about an unidentified modern edition.

recording.value: Rule 3 — territorial: sound recording public domain in the European Union (pre-1963 publication basis).
recording.note: The Internet Archive item carries a CC0 licence URL declared by the uploader, which is not treated as authority to waive Victor’s rights. The pre-1963 European rule applies because the recording was made in 1927 and was on sale by January 1928 (a Victor advertisement in The Golden Book Magazine offers Records Nos. 6663-4-5), so the 50-year term expired before the 2013 extension; the exact first issue date is not established. This is territorial, not a worldwide licence. The recording was published after 1925, so a US public-domain basis is not established.

alternatives.value: Pre-1963 European public domain — territorial basis.
CC0 — licence URL on the Internet Archive item, uploader’s declaration.

rights.creditLine: Franz Schubert, Symphony No. 8 in B minor “Unfinished”, I. Allegro moderato; Philadelphia Orchestra, Leopold Stokowski, April 1927. Victor 6663–6665 (album M-16); transfer by Bob Varney, Internet Archive. Rights metadata conflicts; public domain in the EU only; no worldwide recording clearance is asserted.
